title: ～とか～とか — things like ～ and ～
summary: Lists examples casually: “things like A and B.” It attaches to nouns, verbs and adjectives. It is a spoken form of ～や～など and suggests that there are other items as well.

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ とか ＋ 名詞 ＋ とか
patterns.gloss: noun + とか + noun + とか (パンとか卵とか)

patterns.form: 普通形 ＋ とか ＋ 普通形 ＋ とか
patterns.gloss: verbs and adjectives in plain form can also be listed

body.p: Put とか after each example. The last とか is often kept, as in 掃除とか洗濯とかをします, and a particle such as を, に or が follows it. Two or three examples are typical.
It is casual and a bit vague, which is useful when you do not want to list everything. In formal writing, use ～や～など or ～や～、といった instead. Unlike ～も～も or ～と～, it does not claim the list is complete.

examples.ja: 週末（しゅうまつ）は掃除（そうじ）とか洗濯（せんたく）とかをします。
examples.romaji: Shūmatsu wa sōji toka sentaku toka o shimasu.
examples.tr: On weekends I do things like cleaning and laundry.

examples.ja: 朝（あさ）はパンとか卵（たまご）とかを食（た）べます。
examples.romaji: Asa wa pan toka tamago toka o tabemasu.
examples.tr: In the morning I eat things like bread and eggs.

examples.ja: 休（やす）みの日（ひ）は買（か）い物（もの）とか映画（えいが）とかに行（い）く。
examples.romaji: Yasumi no hi wa kaimono toka eiga toka ni iku.
examples.tr: On my days off I go to places like the shops or the movies.

pitfalls: It is casual. In formal writing, use ～や～など.
Put the particle after the last とか: 掃除とか洗濯とかを, not 掃除とか洗濯をとか.
